_comment: The investigations queue. One topic per generated report, worked through in order and then recycled oldest-first. Add, remove or reorder freely — the generator reads this file every run. 'q' is the reporting question the desk must answer; the sharper it is, the better the piece. Queue order set per editorial/content-audit-2026-08-06.md: health-series completion first, then the elections desk, the reconstruction-money tracker, the West Bank displacement ledger and the sports buildout. Calendar-pegged pieces (UNGA recognition audit, ceasefire day-365, olive harvest) are deliberately NOT queued here — the daily editor adds each one when its window opens, per the audit's calendar table.

topics.en: The ledger of emptied villages: settler violence by name and number
topics.ar: سجلّ القرى المهجَّرة.. عنف المستوطنين بالاسم والرقم
topics.q: Launch of a monthly West Bank displacement ledger (content audit 2026-08-06, rec. C): OCHA's 1,330+ settler-involved attacks since January, the ~1,988 Palestinians displaced in the first four months of 2026, the communities emptied — each by name, date and what stood there — the security cabinet's 1.3-billion-shekel decision for 34 new settlements, and the impunity record (complaints vs indictments, per Yesh Din). Every figure attributed to OCHA, OHCHR, B'Tselem or Yesh Din by report and date; titles and prose name the responsible actors in active voice.

topics.en: Israel budgets 1.3 billion shekels to plant 34 new settlements
topics.ar: إسرائيل ترصد 1.3 مليار شيكل لزرع 34 مستوطنة جديدة
topics.q: Follow the money of the security cabinet's July 2026 decision: 1.3 billion shekels for 34 new settlements — where each is planned, whose land it sits on, which ministries move the funds, and how it connects to the displacement the UN calls an all-time high. Attribute the decision text, budget lines and locations to named documents and outlets; name the deciding officials.

topics.en: The crossing: what Palestinians endure to leave and return
topics.ar: المعابر: ما يتحمّله الفلسطينيون للسفر والعودة
topics.q: Document the Allenby/King Hussein Bridge bottleneck, Rafah's closure, permit regimes, average waiting times, the cost of VIP passage, the denial of an airport since 2001, and the specific rules that govern who may fly from Ben Gurion.

topics.en: Settler attacks and the arithmetic of impunity
topics.ar: اعتداءات المستوطنين وحساب الإفلات من العقاب
topics.q: Using Yesh Din, OCHA and B'Tselem data, what share of Israeli investigations into settler violence end in indictment and conviction? Which outposts recur, what is the documented role of army escorts, and how have sanctions by the EU, UK and US on named settlers played out?

topics.en: The water arithmetic of the West Bank
topics.ar: حساب المياه في الضفة الغربية
topics.q: How much water per capita do Palestinians and settlers receive, how does the Joint Water Committee and Mekorot allocation work, how many cisterns and pipelines have been demolished, and what do B'Tselem and the World Bank report?

topics.en: Building permits in Area C: the paperwork of dispossession
topics.ar: رخص البناء في المنطقة ج
topics.q: What share of Palestinian permit applications in Area C are approved, how many structures — including donor-funded schools and clinics — have been demolished, and what is the documented displacement toll?

topics.en: Revoked: how Jerusalemites lose the right to their city
topics.ar: سحب الإقامة: كيف يفقد المقدسيون حق مدينتهم
topics.q: How does the 'centre of life' rule work, how many residencies have been revoked since 1967, what is happening in Sheikh Jarrah and Silwan, and what is the status of family-unification restrictions?

topics.en: The paperwork of annexation: how West Bank land changes hands
topics.ar: بيروقراطية الضم: كيف تنتقل أراضي الضفة
topics.q: Document the administrative machinery by which West Bank land changes hands, as a system. State land declarations and the acreage by year; retroactive legalisation of outposts; the E1 plan and its status; Area C planning approvals versus Palestinian permit refusals; the transfer of Civil Administration powers to ministerial control; settlement tender, plan and construction figures; road and bypass schemes; firing zones and nature reserves as land designations. Use Peace Now, Kerem Navot, B'Tselem, OCHA and Israeli government publications, and give the source and year for every number.

topics.en: Palestinian football builds on its historic World Cup qualifying run
topics.ar: كرة القدم الفلسطينية تبني على مشوارها المونديالي التاريخي
topics.q: First piece of the sports-section buildout (content audit 2026-08-06, rec. F): where Palestinian football stands after the 2026 World Cup qualification cycle — verify the campaign's final results and records at writing time before stating them — the federation's plans, the West Bank Premier League's attempt to run a season under closure, and Gaza's players a year into the ceasefire. The diaspora's game: what the national team means to Palestinians who have never seen Palestine.

topics.en: The athletes who cannot reach their own matches
topics.ar: رياضيون لا يصلون إلى مبارياتهم
topics.q: Document specific cases of Palestinian athletes denied permits or visas, the state of stadiums and training facilities, and how Palestinian sport is funded.

topics.en: After polio's return: rebuilding Gaza's vaccination shield
topics.ar: بعد عودة شلل الأطفال.. إعادة بناء درع التطعيم في غزة
topics.q: Track the polio detection and campaign history in Gaza since 2024 (WHO/UNICEF rounds, coverage rates). What does routine immunization look like now? Solutions: cold-chain restoration, campaign logistics during access constraints, catch-up schedules.

topics.en: Rebuilding bodies: the rehabilitation system Gaza's wounded need
topics.ar: إعادة بناء الأجساد.. منظومة التأهيل التي يحتاجها جرحى غزة
topics.q: WHO estimates of war-wounded needing long-term rehabilitation; spinal-cord and burn cases. What rehab capacity exists (Sheikh Hamad, ICRC, NGOs), physiotherapist numbers, assistive-device supply. Solutions: rehab-in-community models, training programs, regional partnerships.

topics.en: Palestinians vote on November 28 for the first time in two decades
topics.ar: الفلسطينيون ينتخبون في 28 نوفمبر لأول مرة منذ عقدين
topics.q: Launch report for the Palestinian elections desk (content audit 2026-08-06, rec. A): the PLC election set for 28 November 2026 and the PNC vote the same month, with a presidential vote promised for early 2027. Cover the legal framework and the decrees behind it, voter registration in the West Bank, Gaza and East Jerusalem, the deliberate exclusion of Hamas and Islamic Jihad and the controversy around it with every side carried, the Central Elections Commission's preparations, and the legitimacy question: what an election under occupation and without Gaza's full participation can and cannot confer while the statehood-recognition wave demands one. Attribute every date and rule to the CEC, the specific decree, or the named outlet. This launches a standing desk mirroring the Israeli election watch — same tracker treatment through November.

topics.en: Where is the money? Gaza's reconstruction pledges, tracked line by line
topics.ar: أين الأموال؟.. تعهدات إعمار غزة تحت التدقيق بنداً بنداً
topics.q: Launch of the recurring reconstruction-money tracker (content audit 2026-08-06, rec. B): pledges announced vs money actually transferred to the World Bank-administered fund vs rubble actually cleared (about 0.5% per UN Security Council briefings, May 2026) vs shelters actually built. Name which donors disbursed and which have not, with each figure attributed to the specific UNSC briefing, World Bank report or donor statement and date. Include a house dashboard SVG designed for reuse — this becomes a franchise refreshed as numbers move, in the charter's constructive framing: credit what is delivered precisely, present pending transfers as the next practical stage.

topics.en: Six months on, the Board of Peace still governs Gaza only on paper
topics.ar: بعد ستة أشهر.. «مجلس السلام» يحكم غزة على الورق فقط
topics.q: Standing watch on Gaza's transitional governance (content audit 2026-08-06, rec. B companion): the Board of Peace chaired by President Trump with Nikolay Mladenov as Director-General/High Representative, and the Palestinian technocratic committee (NCAG), both named in January 2026 and neither operational on the ground per UN Security Council briefings. Who sits on each body, what they have actually decided, what authority Palestinians hold inside them, and what fills the vacuum meanwhile. Attribute to the specific UNSC session, named officials and outlets; distinguish established fact from reported-but-unconfirmed.

topics.en: East Jerusalem's ballot boxes again decide whether Palestinians vote
topics.ar: صناديق القدس الشرقية تقرر مجدداً هل ينتخب الفلسطينيون
topics.q: Elections desk: the question that cancelled the 2021 election returns. The Oslo-era arrangements for East Jerusalem voting (post offices, the numbers allowed), Israel's current position, the CEC's plans and fallbacks, what Jerusalemite candidates and voters say, and how each scenario plays into the 28 November vote's legitimacy. Attribute positions to named officials and documents; carry all sides.

topics.en: Which Arab pledges for Gaza actually reached the reconstruction fund
topics.ar: أيُّ التعهدات العربية لغزة وصلت فعلاً إلى صندوق الإعمار؟
topics.q: Arab Support edition of the money tracker: summit by summit, which Arab pledges for Gaza reconstruction have actually transferred to the World Bank-administered fund or disbursed bilaterally, which are pending, and what each donor government says about timing. Charter framing applies: precise credit for what is delivered and funded, pending transfers presented as the next practical stage, never insinuation — and every figure attributed to the donor statement, fund report or UNSC briefing that carries it.

topics.en: The draft constitution redraws the Palestinian political system
topics.ar: مسودة الدستور تعيد رسم النظام السياسي الفلسطيني
topics.q: Explainer for the elections desk: the new draft constitution clause by clause — what changes from the Basic Law, presidential vs parliamentary powers, the judiciary, rights provisions, how it handles the PLO-PA relationship and statehood, and who wrote it under what mandate. What critics and supporters each say, attributed by name. Written as a reader's guide: what each clause means in practice.

topics.en: Gaza's children begin a third school year without schools
topics.ar: أطفال غزة يدخلون عامهم الدراسي الثالث بلا مدارس
topics.q: The September 1 school-year package (content audit 2026-08-06, rec. D): 658,000 school-age children, 60% with no in-person learning, 92% of schools needing reconstruction or major rehabilitation, UNICEF's Back to Learning reaching 336,000, and 335,000 under-fives at risk of severe developmental delay — every number attributed to UNICEF, PCHR or the ETF by report and date. Solutions lens per the health-series model: the tent classrooms, the remote-degree workarounds, who teaches and how teachers are paid. Cross-link the scholarship guide as the service layer.

topics.en: Gaza's university students fight to finish degrees frozen by war
topics.ar: طلبة جامعات غزة يقاتلون لإتمام شهادات جمّدتها الحرب
topics.q: The higher-education layer of the lost-school-years story: students mid-degree when the universities were destroyed — what remote and partnership programs exist, which foreign universities took transfers, what the scholarship guide's programs cover, and the students rebuilding study circles in the rubble. Solutions lens; names and campuses verified; cross-link the scholarship guide.

topics.en: Nine million diaspora Palestinians wait to learn how they vote
topics.ar: تسعة ملايين فلسطيني في الشتات ينتظرون معرفة كيف سيقترعون
topics.q: Elections desk: the Palestine National Council vote planned for November is the diaspora's first chance at representation in decades. How PNC seats are meant to be filled, whether refugees in Lebanon, Jordan, Syria and the wider diaspora actually get ballots, what registration exists, and what diaspora communities say. The launch report's diaspora companion; attribute the rules to the specific PLO/PNC decisions and carry the skeptics.

topics.en: One family returns to Rafah between a war and a peace
topics.ar: عائلة تعود إلى رفح بين حربٍ لم تنتهِ وسلامٍ لم يبدأ
topics.q: Real Lives: follow one family's return to Rafah through the ceasefire's 'neither war nor peace' — what they found, what they rebuilt first, where water and school and work come from now. Their words lead; our summary follows (charter rule). The piece that gives the tracker numbers a face without spectacle.

topics.en: Commerce returns to Gaza's tent cities one stall at a time
topics.ar: التجارة تعود إلى مدن الخيام في غزة بسطةً بعد بسطة
topics.q: The shelter-city economy: markets among the tents — prices, cash scarcity and damaged banknotes, who extends credit, what work pays, remittances' role. Ground reporting register with numbers attributed to named traders, the PCBS or UN assessments. Pairs with the humans Rafah piece and the money tracker.

topics.en: A developmental emergency stalks Gaza's 335,000 youngest children
topics.ar: طوارئ نمائية تهدد 335 ألف طفل دون الخامسة في غزة
topics.q: Health series follow-on flagged in the September education package: UNICEF's warning that 335,000 children under five risk severe developmental delay after early-childhood services collapsed. What early-childhood care existed before the war, what remains, the science of the first thousand days told plainly, and the interventions working now — attribute to UNICEF and named clinicians; solutions lens per the series.

topics.en: The machinery that must deliver a Palestinian election in November
topics.ar: الآلة الانتخابية التي يجب أن تنجز اقتراع نوفمبر
topics.q: Follow-up to the elections-desk launch: the nuts and bolts. Voter rolls and how current they are, polling infrastructure in a destroyed Gaza, the courts that adjudicate disputes, election observation (who is invited, who is barred), campaign finance rules, and what the CEC says it still lacks. Compare against what broke in the cancelled 2021 cycle. Attribute to the CEC, named officials and outlets.

topics.en: How the diaspora actually gets money into Gaza and the West Bank
topics.ar: كيف يوصل المغتربون أموالهم فعلاً إلى غزة والضفة؟
topics.q: Service guide (content audit 2026-08-06, rec. H — evergreen reference the daily editor keeps current): the remittance channels that actually work into Gaza and the West Bank in 2026, fees and limits, bank vs exchange-house vs aid-platform routes, and reader protection: how to verify a channel before sending. Everything phrased verify-at-source. The crypto/ecash angle belongs to the Financial Freedom desk's layer — reference its coverage inline rather than duplicating it.

topics.en: Saint Levant raps for a Gaza he cannot enter
topics.ar: سان ليفانت يغني الراب لغزةٍ لا يستطيع دخولها
topics.q: Report Saint Levant's story for the Palestinian-rise series: Gaza birth, Jerusalem and Amman upbringing, trilingual rap, From Gaza and 5am in Paris, the Coachella performances with Palestinian imagery, his Gaza fundraising. Attribute streams/charts and quotes to outlets.

topics.en: Elyanna carries Nazareth's voice to Coachella's main stages
topics.ar: إليانا تحمل صوت الناصرة إلى مسارح كوتشيلا
topics.q: Report Elyanna's arc for the arts desk's Palestinian-rise series (launched with the Mohammed Assaf profile): Nazareth childhood, the move to LA, becoming the first artist to perform a full Arabic-language set at Coachella, her albums and collaborations, how she carries Palestinian identity on global stages during the war. Attribute chart facts and quotes to specific outlets. FRAMING (owner order 2026-08-05): this is a celebratory FEATURE for the culture pages — warm, proud, the artist's achievement at the center. No gotcha angles; never frame exile or absence from Palestine as contradiction or hypocrisy — the war and closure keep Palestinians from home. Any controversy is brief fair context with her side carried, never the lede or headline.

topics.en: Sama' Abdulhadi takes Ramallah's techno underground to the world's festivals
topics.ar: سما عبد الهادي تنقل تكنو رام الله إلى مهرجانات العالم
topics.q: Report Sama' Abdulhadi's arc for the Palestinian-rise series: Ramallah scene origins, the Boiler Room set that traveled the world, the 2020 Nabi Musa arrest controversy and release, international festival career, what performing as 'Palestine's techno queen' means during the war. Attribute precisely. FRAMING (owner order 2026-08-05): this is a celebratory FEATURE for the culture pages — warm, proud, the artist's achievement at the center. No gotcha angles; never frame exile or absence from Palestine as contradiction or hypocrisy — the war and closure keep Palestinians from home. Any controversy is brief fair context with her side carried, never the lede or headline.

topics.en: Bitchat's mesh spreads worldwide as blackout-proof messaging matures
topics.ar: شبكة «بيتشات» تنتشر عالمياً كمراسلةٍ عصيّة على الانقطاع
topics.q: Where is bitchat being adopted around the world in 2026 — disasters, protests, blackout regions — what do its latest releases add, and what does each development mean practically for Palestinians whose internet and phone service come and go? Include the official download sources (App Store 'bitchat mesh'; permissionlesstech GitHub APK) and the Google Play impostor warning.

topics.en: In St. Louis, a Palestinian dance troupe turns dabke into support for autistic children in the West Bank
topics.ar: في سانت لويس.. فرقة دبكة فلسطينية ترقص لأجل أطفال التوحد في الضفة
topics.q: Report the story of Hanan Hamed and her St. Louis dance troupe Canaan Wellspring, whose 'Jafra' performance on August 1, 2026 (Purser Center, Logan University, Chesterfield, Missouri) explores regional dabke styles and benefits her nonprofit Autism Superhero Palestine, which supports autistic children and their families in the West Bank. St. Louis Public Radio covered it. Research the troupe, the nonprofit's work in the West Bank, what services exist (and don't) for autistic Palestinian children under occupation, and the wider phenomenon of diaspora arts fundraising. The frame is the system: cultural preservation as community infrastructure, and the gap in disability services it is trying to fill.

topics.en: Where the money actually goes: the Palestinian Authority budget, line by line
topics.ar: إلى أين تذهب الأموال فعلاً: موازنة السلطة الفلسطينية بنداً بنداً
topics.q: Work through the Palestinian Ministry of Finance's published budget and monthly fiscal reports line by line. What are total revenues — domestic tax, clearance revenue, donor grants — and where does expenditure actually go: the wage bill by sector, the security sector's share, health and education, social transfers, net lending to utilities, debt service and arrears to the private sector and the pension fund? Give every figure with the document, year and currency it came from, and say where figures are not comparable across years. How has the composition changed since budget support collapsed, and what is the deficit resting on now?

topics.en: Thousands of new amputees, and the prosthetics pipeline meant to reach them
topics.ar: آلاف مبتوري الأطراف الجدد.. أين وصلت سلسلة الأطراف الصناعية؟
topics.q: How many Gazans lost limbs in the war (OCHA/WHO/UNICEF counts)? Map the prosthetics pipeline: who fits limbs today (Hamad hospital's artificial limbs center, ICRC, Jordanian field hospitals, medical evacuation programs), waiting times, pediatric refitting needs as children grow, 3D-printed and low-cost limb initiatives, and what a scaled solution would look like. Solutions framing: what works, what it costs, who is funding it, what is missing.

topics.en: Cancer care in Gaza collapsed. Where do patients go now?
topics.ar: انهار علاج السرطان في غزة.. إلى أين يذهب المرضى؟
topics.q: Before the war, where did Gaza's cancer patients get treatment (Turkish-Palestinian Friendship Hospital, referrals to East Jerusalem/Egypt/Jordan)? What exists now: medical evacuation numbers, referral backlogs, which countries take patients, chemotherapy availability. Solutions: evacuation corridors, telemedicine oncology consults, rebuilding oncology capacity — who is proposing what and what it would take.

topics.en: Telemedicine as a lifeline: connecting Gaza's patients to the world's doctors
topics.ar: الطب عن بُعد شريان حياة يصل مرضى غزة بأطباء العالم
topics.q: Which telemedicine programs actually operate for Gaza and the West Bank (diaspora physician networks, Sahara-style volunteer platforms, hospital twinning)? What do they treat, what are the connectivity and power constraints, what results are documented? Solutions: what infrastructure (satellite internet, solar) and licensing changes would scale it.

topics.en: A generation in trauma: mental health care for Gaza's children
topics.ar: جيل تحت الصدمة.. الصحة النفسية لأطفال غزة
topics.q: What do UNICEF/WHO/GCMHP assessments say about PTSD and trauma prevalence among Gaza's children? What treatment capacity exists (Gaza Community Mental Health Programme, school-based programs, remote counseling)? Solutions: community-level psychosocial models proven in other war zones, training pipelines, funding gaps.

topics.en: Chronic illness under siege: keeping dialysis and insulin flowing
topics.ar: المرض المزمن تحت الحصار.. كيف يستمر الغسيل الكلوي والأنسولين؟
topics.q: How many dialysis patients and insulin-dependent diabetics does Gaza have, per WHO? What happened to them during the war; what is the machine/generator/supply status now? Solutions: solar-powered dialysis units, cold-chain insulin logistics, home peritoneal dialysis — who has piloted what.

topics.en: Giving birth in the rubble: maternal and newborn care in Gaza
topics.ar: الولادة بين الركام.. صحة الأمهات والمواليد في غزة
topics.q: What are current maternal and neonatal outcomes vs prewar (UNFPA/WHO data)? Functioning maternity capacity, midwife networks, incubator/NICU status. Solutions: mobile maternity units, midwife-led community birthing, kangaroo care programs — evidence and funders.

topics.en: How much donor aid reaches Palestinians, and how much never leaves the donor
topics.ar: كم من المساعدات يصل الفلسطينيين وكم لا يغادر الجهة المانحة أصلاً
topics.q: Which donors give what, through which mechanism — direct budget support, the EU's PEGASE, UNRWA, project aid, or spending administered by the donor's own agencies and contractors? Using OECD DAC data, EU and World Bank AHLC reports and Palestinian Ministry of Finance figures, establish how much reaches the Palestinian treasury versus how much is spent by the donor before it ever arrives. Cite each figure to its document and year. Track the fall in direct budget support since 2013 and what replaced it.

topics.en: From de-development to depopulation: testing the framework against the record
topics.ar: من تدمير التنمية إلى التهجير: اختبار الإطار على أرض الواقع
topics.q: Sara Roy's scholarship argues Gaza's economy was deliberately de-developed rather than merely underdeveloped — structurally prevented from functioning. Test that framework against the current record across Gaza and the West Bank, and ask what has changed. Assemble the data: GDP, employment and trade figures, movement and import restrictions, land and water access, OCHA demolition and displacement counts, housing destruction, and recorded population movement. Identify the mechanisms and the actors, and where a strategy is stated in a published plan or an official's on-the-record statement, quote the document. Then report what this does to ordinary life — work, school, water, burial, staying put. Attribute every claim of intent to the document that contains it; where intent is contested or unstated, report the effect and say the intent is not established.

topics.en: Every published proposal to move Gaza's population, and what the law says
topics.ar: كل خطة منشورة لتهجير سكان غزة وما يقوله القانون
topics.q: Catalogue the published proposals concerning the movement of Gaza's population: who authored each, what it proposes, how it was funded or promoted, and what officials have said about it on the record in their official capacity. Set against them the documented displacement figures, the share of housing stock destroyed, and where people have actually moved. Then report what the ICJ, UN special rapporteurs, the ICRC and named legal scholars have said about forcible transfer and the conditions that make departure coerced. Report the documents and the law and nothing beyond them.

topics.en: Who is actually making money in the Palestinian economy
topics.ar: من يجني الأموال فعلياً في الاقتصاد الفلسطيني
topics.q: Which families, holding companies and monopolies dominate Palestinian commerce — PADICO, Paltel/Jawwal, cement and fuel importers, the Palestine Investment Fund? Who owns them, what are their margins, how concentrated is ownership, and who sits on both the boards and the political bodies that regulate them?

topics.en: Deaths in Palestinian custody and what accountability followed
topics.ar: الوفيات في مراكز الاحتجاز الفلسطينية وما تلاها من مساءلة
topics.q: How many deaths in PA and Hamas custody have been documented by the Independent Commission for Human Rights and Al-Haq, and what followed each: an investigation, a published finding, a trial, a verdict? The Nizar Banat case is the best-documented example — track the procedural record of that trial as published, how long it has run and where it stands. Report the accountability gap as the finding; do not name officers or assign guilt.

topics.en: The committees that were formed and never reported
topics.ar: لجان شُكّلت ولم تُصدر تقريراً قط
topics.q: Catalogue Palestinian investigative and reform committees announced since 2005 that never published findings — deaths in custody, the 2007 events, pension and public-sector reform, electricity arrears, PIF audits. Which body formed each, what were the published terms of reference and deadline, and what has been published since? The finding is the pattern of non-delivery, not any individual.

topics.en: The rules on officials and business, and whether anyone enforces them
topics.ar: قواعد تضارب المصالح ومن يطبّقها
topics.q: What law governs conflict of interest, asset declaration and outside business interests for Palestinian public officials? Is declaration mandatory, is it published, who audits it, and what has the Anti-Corruption Commission, the State Audit Bureau or AMAN's Transparency reports found about compliance? Report the rules and the enforcement record as a system — name no private individuals.

topics.en: The brokers who sell Israeli work permits
topics.ar: سماسرة تصاريح العمل
topics.q: How does the Israeli work-permit market for Palestinian labourers function, what do brokers charge, how much of a worker's wage is skimmed, who profits on both sides of the Green Line, and what have the Bank of Israel, Kav LaOved and Palestinian labour ministries documented?

topics.en: The money Israel collects and withholds
topics.ar: الأموال التي تجبيها إسرائيل وتحتجزها
topics.q: How does the Paris Protocol clearance-revenue mechanism work, how much has Israel deducted or withheld and on what legal basis, what has that done to PA salaries and the banking system, and what have the IMF, World Bank and PMA reported?

topics.en: The aid economy: who profits from Palestinian need
topics.ar: اقتصاد المساعدات: من يربح من الحاجة الفلسطينية
topics.q: Which contractors, security firms, logistics companies and consultancies capture humanitarian and development spending for Palestinians, what overheads do they take, and what have audits by donor governments found?

topics.en: Held without charge: administrative detention by the numbers
topics.ar: الاعتقال الإداري بالأرقام
topics.q: How many Palestinians are held without charge, including children, under what military orders, for how long on average, and what have HaMoked, Addameer, the ICRC and UN bodies documented about conditions and deaths in custody?

topics.en: The deadliest place to be a reporter
topics.ar: أخطر مكان لممارسة الصحافة
topics.q: How many Palestinian journalists have been killed, by whom, and how many killings produced an investigation or charge? Use CPJ, RSF and IFJ counts, and cover press-freedom pressure from the PA and Hamas as well.

topics.en: The law used to arrest Palestinians for posting
topics.ar: القانون الذي يُعتقل به الفلسطينيون بسبب منشور
topics.q: How has the PA's cybercrime decree been used against journalists, students and critics, how many prosecutions, what do Palestinian bar associations and rights groups say, and how does Hamas police speech in Gaza?

topics.en: Palestinian citizens of Israel: the second front
topics.ar: فلسطينيو الداخل: الجبهة الثانية
topics.q: Cover the Kaminitz Law, unrecognised Naqab/Negev villages and demolitions, the Nakba Law, policing and organised crime deaths in Arab towns, and political representation.

topics.en: What happens if UNRWA stops
topics.ar: ماذا لو توقفت الأونروا
topics.q: Trace the defunding decisions, the Israeli legislation banning UNRWA operations, the Colonna review findings, how many schools, clinics and rations are at stake, and what contingency exists.

topics.en: Cameras, checkpoints and code: surveillance of Palestinians

A humans-forward economy piece: one crew's day at sea carries the reporting. Attribute zone limits and incidents to named sources.

topics.q: How many olive trees have been uprooted or burned, how does the coordination system for harvest access work, what share of the rural economy depends on olives, and what do farming unions report?

topics.q: How are Palestinian films funded and distributed, what happened to filmmakers and cinemas in Gaza, and what pressure have festivals and distributors faced?

topics.q: How do correspondent banking withdrawal, PayPal exclusion, frozen accounts and the shekel cash glut restrict Palestinians, what workarounds are actually in use, and what have the PMA, HRF and researchers documented about bitcoin adoption in the territories?

topics.q: Compare the published post-war governance proposals from the US, Arab states, Israel, the PA and think tanks — who governs, who polices, who pays, and what do Palestinians say about being consulted?

topics.en: The $400 million the Gaza roadmap owes contractors, and who verifies the claims
topics.ar: 400 مليون دولار في خارطة غزة للمتعاقدين.. من يدقّق المطالبات؟
topics.q: The Board of Peace disarmament roadmap published on 31 July 2026 commits the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza to honour legitimate commitments to suppliers and contractors up to $400 million as part of an audit to be completed within three years. Report the substance behind that figure: who is owed money in Gaza — construction firms, fuel importers, medical suppliers, municipal contractors, wholesalers — for what, by whom (Hamas-era ministries, the PA, UN agencies, the Board of Peace itself), and how large are the arrears by any documented estimate. Who will adjudicate claims, under what evidentiary standard, and what happens to creditors above the ceiling or with records destroyed in the war? Attribute every figure to a document, ministry, chamber of commerce or audit and say where no reliable figure exists.

topics.en: How to verify a Gaza donation appeal before you give
topics.ar: كيف تتحقق من حملة تبرعات لغزة قبل أن تتبرع؟
topics.q: Service guide (content audit 2026-08-06, rec. H — reader protection, kept current by the daily editor): how a reader can verify a Gaza or West Bank donation appeal before giving — which registries and audit trails exist (charity regulators, GoFundMe-style platform verification, the established NGOs' own reporting), the red flags of a fraudulent appeal, and how established Palestinian-serving organizations differ in what they can actually deliver into Gaza. Name no suspected fraudster without a named source on the record; the guide protects readers by teaching verification, not by accusation. Everything phrased verify-at-source.

topics.en: The papers that rule Palestinian lives, explained one by one
topics.ar: الأوراق التي تحكم حياة الفلسطينيين.. وثيقةً وثيقة
topics.q: Service reference (content audit 2026-08-06, rec. H): the document system Palestinians live under, explained plainly — the West Bank/Gaza ID and Israel's population registry control, East Jerusalem permanent residency and its revocation rules, family reunification's frozen queue, travel documents by host country for refugees, and what each recognition of Palestinian statehood changed (or did not) for passports. Every rule attributed to the issuing authority or the named rights organization documenting it; pairs with the queued jerusalem-residency topic; phrased verify-at-source.

topics.en: Widowed women now head Gaza's households and its rebuilding
topics.ar: أرامل غزة يرأسن البيوت ويقدن إعادة الإعمار
topics.q: Her Story (pipeline commitment, content audit 2026-08-06): the war left tens of thousands of women heading households — verify the current UN Women/OCHA estimate at writing. How women-headed families navigate the tent economy, aid registration, inheritance and guardianship rules, and the work women do to hold families together (charter: her words lead, our summary follows; every finding attributed to the specific UN body and date; no spectacle).

topics.en: Women teachers run the tent classrooms of Gaza's lost school years
topics.ar: معلّمات يُدرن صفوف الخيام في سنوات غزة الدراسية الضائعة
topics.q: Her Story companion to the September education package: the women running Gaza's tent classrooms and learning circles — who they are, how they are (or are not) paid, what UNICEF's Back to Learning assigns them, and what teaching through displacement costs and gives them. Consent and safety rules apply in full; names only with clear consent; attribute program facts to UNICEF/UNRWA by report and date.

topics.en: Britain answers — or a court is asked to make it
topics.ar: بريطانيا تردّ على عريضة بلفور أو يتولّى القضاء إلزامها
topics.q: Standing follow-up to masri-britain-owes-palestine-2026: the Britain Owes Palestine campaign has given Keir Starmer's government until September 2026 to answer the 400-page petition delivered to 10 Downing Street in September 2025 (drafted by Ben Emmerson KC and Danny Friedman KC; delivered by Munib al-Masri with his grandson, Avi Shlaim and Victor Kattan). Cover the government's response the day it lands, or the judicial-review application if the deadline passes — what the filing says, which court, what remedies it seeks, first hearing dates. Same-day both languages; attribute every filing and statement to the named document, lawyer or outlet; carry the government's side.

topics.en: Can a British court judge the Balfour Declaration?
topics.ar: هل تستطيع محكمة بريطانية محاكمة وعد بلفور؟
topics.q: Researched legal explainer ahead of the Britain Owes Palestine judicial-review decision: the petition's legal theory (Britain unlawfully failed to recognise Arab self-determination; lacked legal authority for the Declaration and the Mandate), what judicial review can and cannot reach for pre-1948 state acts, the Mau Mau (Kenya) settlement and Chagos litigation as precedents for historical-wrong claims against the UK, the archives question (what the FCDO still holds), and the scholars on both sides — Kattan and Shlaim for the petition, and the strongest good-faith counterarguments beside them. Distinguish what is legally arguable, politically possible and historically established; attribute every position to a named lawyer, ruling or document.

topics.en: Chronic illness inside Israeli detention, and the medicine that stops at the gate
topics.ar: المرض المزمن خلف القضبان.. الدواء الذي يتوقف عند بوابة السجن
topics.q: How does Israeli detention handle Palestinians whose illnesses require continuous treatment? Build the record from named sources: Physicians for Human Rights-Israel and Addameer casework, Israel Prison Service and military responses, and documented files including the Palestinian-American Birzeit student Sama Safi, held without charge since 2 June 2026 with familial Mediterranean fever requiring daily medication and a quarterly injection available only outside the country. Establish what treatment the law requires, what detainees actually receive, which conditions (dialysis, cancer, diabetes, autoimmune disease) fare worst, and what the record shows in documented deaths in custody. Attribute every figure to a named organisation, report and date; carry the Israeli authorities' responses; report the issue, never the individual, and publish no medical detail a family has not made public.

topics.en: Who commands the foreign force entering Gaza, and who answers for it
topics.ar: من يقود القوة الأجنبية الداخلة إلى غزة.. ومن يُسأل عنها؟
topics.q: Map the International Stabilization Force before it deploys. Establish the mandate from Security Council resolution 2803 of November 2025 and its two-year clock, the American commander Maj. Gen. Jasper Jeffers, every pledging state and the size of its contingent (Indonesia's up-to-8,000 offer and deputy-commander role, Morocco, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Albania; Egypt and Jordan on police training), the Rafah-first sector plan, the 20,000-troop and 12,000-police targets, and who pays. Then answer the question the roadmap leaves open: if a soldier of this force kills or injures a Palestinian, which court hears it, which complaint route exists, which immunity applies — and what the precedents (UNIFIL in Lebanon, the MFO in Sinai, the 1982-84 Beirut multinational force) tell Palestinians to expect. Attribute every mandate, pledge and legal provision to the named resolution, official statement or agreement text.

topics.en: Freed Palestinian women recount detention in their own words
topics.ar: أسيرات محرّرات يروين تجربة الاعتقال بكلماتهنّ
topics.q: Her Story (section-freshness queue, owner order 2026-08-11): accounts of Palestinian women released from Israeli detention in 2025-26, built on published testimonies with the section's consent-and-safety rules binding — never name a survivor of sexual violence without explicit consent; anonymous accounts run. Attribute counts of women detainees to نادي الأسير / هيئة شؤون الأسرى with dates; attribute documented abuse findings to the specific UN body and report. Her words lead; our summary follows.

topics.en: Gaza's midwives deliver a generation through the war
topics.ar: قابلات غزة يولّدن جيلاً وسط الحرب
topics.q: Her Story: midwives and maternal care in Gaza now — births during the ceasefire period, UNFPA/OCHA maternal-health figures verified at writing, the midwife networks operating outside destroyed hospitals, and what women themselves describe. Complements the health section's maternal-care coverage; the women are the subject, not the illustration.

topics.en: UN reports document violence against Palestinian women in custody
topics.ar: تقارير أممية توثق العنف ضد الفلسطينيات في الاحتجاز
topics.q: Her Story: what UN bodies have documented in 2025-26 on sexual and gender-based violence against Palestinian women in detention, at checkpoints and by settlers — every finding attributed to the specific body, report and date (Commission of Inquiry, OHCHR, UN Women); Israeli responses carried; no survivor identified without consent.

topics.en: West Bank widows hold family economies together after the raids
topics.ar: أرامل الضفة يمسكن اقتصاد البيوت بعد الاقتحامات
topics.q: Her Story: women who head West Bank households after husbands were killed or detained — inheritance and guardianship hurdles, work, aid registration, the institutions that help; figures attributed to PCBS/UN Women with dates.

topics.en: Palestine's national football team plays its home games in exile
topics.ar: منتخب فلسطين يخوض مبارياته «البيتية» في الملاعب البعيدة
topics.q: Sports: the national team's current competitive position verified at writing (Asian qualifiers standing, recent results, where 'home' fixtures are actually played and why), the players' routes out of Gaza and the West Bank, and what the federation says. Celebrate the sporting story; the closure that denies home games is reported precisely.

topics.en: Gaza's athletes return to training grounds the war left standing
topics.ar: رياضيو غزة يعودون إلى التدريب فوق ما تركته الحرب
topics.q: Sports: which clubs, gyms and pitches in Gaza function now; the Palestine Olympic Committee's account of athletes killed and facilities destroyed (attributed with dates); the tournaments restarting in the ceasefire period; individual athletes' comebacks told celebratorily per the features rule.

topics.en: Palestinian women's football keeps its league running against the odds

topics.q: Sports x Her Story: the women's league and national team — current season status verified at writing, the clubs that carry it, pioneering players and coaches profiled celebratorily; obstacles (movement, funding, facilities) reported factually.

topics.en: Administrative detention holds thousands of Palestinians without charge
topics.ar: الاعتقال الإداري يحتجز آلاف الفلسطينيين بلا تهمة
topics.q: Prisoners desk launch report: the current administrative detention count attributed to نادي الأسير / هيئة شؤون الأسرى with exact dates; how the renewal mechanism works; the legal challenges; family accounts within report-the-issue rules. This is the section's foundational explainer.

topics.en: Israel holds hundreds of Palestinian children in its prisons
topics.ar: إسرائيل تحتجز مئات الأطفال الفلسطينيين في سجونها
topics.q: Prisoners: minors in Israeli detention — counts attributed to DCIP and the prisoners' institutions with dates, the military court track for children, documented conditions per specific reports, releases in exchanges. Report the issue, never the individual child without guardian consent.

topics.en: Washington keeps no public ledger of what it shipped Israel this year
topics.ar: واشنطن لا تنشر سجلاً بما شحنته من سلاح لإسرائيل هذا العام
topics.q: Accountability: reconstruct what the United States has actually delivered to Israel since the Iran war began — Foreign Military Sales notifications with their dates, the January 2026 package worth $6.67bn, and the April 2026 Senate disapproval votes (bulldozers 40-59, 1,000-pound bombs 36 in favour). Set that against the munitions shortage the Pentagon now concedes: the CSIS interceptor estimates, Feinberg's 5 August memo giving arms makers 21 days, and the stopgap that withheld authority for five multiyear munitions contracts. Attribute every figure to the specific notification, roll call or named analyst with its date, and state plainly where no public accounting exists.

topics.en: Clearing Gaza's 68 million tonnes of rubble carries its own health cost
topics.ar: إزالة 68 مليون طن من ركام غزة تحمل كلفتها الصحية
topics.q: Health: report the public-health side of Gaza's rubble removal, the physical precondition of every reconstruction plan Washington and the Board of Peace discuss. Establish with attributed sources what the debris contains — asbestos from older roofing, pulverised concrete dust, unexploded ordnance, human remains — citing UNEP, UNMAS, WHO and the Palestinian Environment Quality Authority by report and date. Then report what protection exists for the workers and for the families living beside the piles: masks and wetting, screening, clinics able to follow respiratory illness over years, and where trained clearance capacity comes from. Give precise credit for programmes already funded and running, and separate what is promised from what is underway and what is still needed.

topics.en: Can Palestinians pay for anything without an Israeli correspondent bank?
topics.ar: هل يستطيع الفلسطينيون الدفع من دون مصرف إسرائيلي مراسل؟
topics.q: Economy: test, mechanism by mechanism, what still settles if the Israeli correspondent channel closes on 1 September and 1 October, when Israel Discount Bank and Bank Hapoalim have said they will stop clearing Palestinian shekel transactions. Establish the baseline first — Reuters put the volume at 51 billion shekels a year, about $16.6bn, with roughly 90 per cent of Palestinian trade passing through Israel — then take each alternative in turn and say precisely where it depends on the same channel: the e-wallets (PalPay, JawwalPay; the Atlantic Council's Melanie Robbins recorded transactions rising from $40m to $115m in early 2025), Jordanian-dinar accounts and the Jordanian banking route, the Palestine Monetary Authority's own clearing capacity and its lack of a currency, cash importation and the physical-shekel surplus that West Bank vaults already hold, and Arab or multilateral deposits and guarantees offered to the PMA. Ask specifically what happens to the payment chains ordinary life runs on: importers of medicine and fuel, aid organisations paying Gaza staff, municipal salaries, and university fees. Every figure attributed to the PMA, Reuters, the World Bank, the IMF or a named analyst with its date; state plainly which questions no public source answers, and keep the actors named in active voice — this is a set of Israeli commercial and ministerial decisions, not a weather event.

topics.en: The water run: how a Gaza family fills its jerrycans each day
topics.ar: مشوار الماء اليومي.. هكذا تملأ عائلة في غزة صفائحها
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable whenever the humans section runs dry; research FRESH developments each time. The daily water economy of the strip under the ceasefire: liters per person against the WHO emergency minimum, desalination and trucking capacity now (attribute to UNICEF/OCHA/PWA by report and date), the price of a cubic meter this month, who in the family carries, how far, and what the queue costs in school hours. One family's documented day carries the piece; numbers attributed inline. Issue-not-individual discipline; both editions composed separately.

topics.en: Gaza's night shift keeps the strip alive until morning
topics.ar: وردية الليل في غزة تُبقي القطاع حياً حتى الصباح
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable; research fresh each run. The people who work while Gaza sleeps: bakers firing ovens for the dawn queue, emergency-room nurses and ambulance crews, generator and network technicians keeping phones alive, fishermen leaving before first light under the naval closure. What each shift pays, what it risks, attributed to the workers' own institutions (bakers' union, hospital directorates, PALTEL updates, fishermen's committees) with dates. Wire-service register, 1-3 sentence paragraphs, no composite characters — only named or explicitly anonymized real people from sourced reporting.

topics.en: What Arab reconstruction pledges actually disbursed this quarter
topics.ar: ماذا صُرف فعلاً من التعهدات العربية لإعمار غزة هذا الفصل
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable quarterly or whenever the arabaid section runs dry. The pledge-to-disbursement ledger: for each major Arab commitment (Cairo summit reconstruction framework, Gulf field hospitals and fuel grants, scholarship programs, medical corridors), what was promised, what reached Gaza or the West Bank since the last check, through which channel, and what stalled — every figure attributed to the funding body, UN tracker or recipient institution by name and date. Charter constructive-framing rule applies: credit delivered work precisely, present pending tranches as the next practical stage, never insinuate bad faith without evidence.

topics.en: Prison visits ration Palestinian families to minutes a year
topics.ar: زيارات السجون تقنّن لقاء العائلات الفلسطينية بدقائق في السنة
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable whenever the prisoners section runs dry. The visits regime as it stands now: ICRC family-visit program status (suspended/resumed, attribute to ICRC statements by date), which prisons allow visits and at what interval, permit refusal patterns for West Bank and Gaza families, the bus routes and hours a single visit costs, and lawyers' access as the fallback channel. Numbers to نادي الأسير / هيئة شؤون الأسرى / ICRC by institution and date; a female prisoner's case keeps Her Story consent rules. Report the issue, never spectacle.

topics.en: Checkpoints tax every West Bank workday in hours and shekels
topics.ar: الحواجز تفرض ضريبتها اليومية على الضفة وقتاً ومالاً
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable; research fresh each run. The checkpoint system as a daily economic fact: how many fixed and flying checkpoints this month (OCHA movement-and-access data by report and date), the pre-dawn labor queues, what a commute costs in hours and shekels, the permit regime's current state, and what closures did to this month's trade. Numbers to OCHA/PCBS/the Palestinian employers' and workers' unions, named and dated. Active-voice discipline: Israel operates the checkpoints — say so.

topics.en: Villages organize night watches as settler raids continue
topics.ar: القرى تنظّم حراسات ليلية مع استمرار اعتداءات المستوطنين
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable. The community-protection file: which villages keep organized night watches now, what a watch shift looks like, the alert networks between villages, documented raids in the past weeks (OCHA/B'Tselem/Yesh Din by date), and what protection the PA and Israeli army did or did not provide in each named case. Follows the Qusra-file discipline: attribute every incident, carry official answers where given, never imply guilt without record.

topics.en: Diaspora remittances hold Palestinian households through the war economy
topics.ar: تحويلات المغتربين تسند بيوت الفلسطينيين في اقتصاد الحرب
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable. The remittance lifeline by the numbers: World Bank/PMA flows this year vs last (by release and date), what a Gaza or West Bank family pays in transfer fees and cash-out premiums, the routes that still work when banks don't, and diaspora fundraising campaigns that verifiably delivered. Constructive-framing rule for the campaigns: credit delivered work precisely, distinguish promised/funded/delivered.

topics.en: The second generation carries Palestine into new professions abroad
topics.ar: الجيل الثاني يحمل فلسطين إلى مهن جديدة في المهجر
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable; celebrate-the-subject rule binds (owner order 2026-08-05). Rotating profile territory: children of the diaspora entering fields where Palestinians were absent — judges, orchestra chairs, research labs, national teams — with the achievement as the story and exile told with empathy from the subject's side. Each recycle picks a fresh, verifiable subject with rights-cleared imagery; never re-profile the same person within a year.

topics.en: Arab universities absorb Gaza's stranded students by the thousand
topics.ar: جامعات عربية تستوعب آلاف طلبة غزة العالقين
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable each semester. The education corridor: which Arab universities enrolled Gaza and West Bank students this term, scholarship counts and terms (by university/ministry announcement and date), credit-transfer and document problems solved or pending, and student voices through their unions. Verify-at-source phrasing for every deadline; constructive framing with precise credit.

topics.en: Palestinian culture rebuilds its stages one reopening at a time
topics.ar: الثقافة الفلسطينية تعيد بناء منصاتها افتتاحاً بعد افتتاح
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable. The cultural-infrastructure ledger: theatres, galleries, music schools and libraries damaged or destroyed (attribute to ministry/UNESCO assessments by date) set against every documented reopening, new company, festival edition or touring production this season. Celebrate-the-subject register for the makers; precise attribution for the damage record.

topics.en: Released prisoners rebuild lives the prison years interrupted
topics.ar: الأسرى المحررون يرمّمون حياة قطعتها سنوات الأسر
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable. The after-release file: how many released this quarter (نادي الأسير/هيئة شؤون الأسرى by statement and date), the health conditions documented on release, re-arrest patterns, the PA's reintegration stipends and their payment state, and one released prisoner's rebuilt routine told with consent. Her Story consent rules bind for women; report the issue, never spectacle.

topics.en: The Gaza committee holds portfolios but controls little money
topics.ar: اللجنة الوطنية لإدارة غزة تحمل الحقائب ولا تملك المال
topics.q: The National Committee for the Administration of Gaza was formed in January 2026 under UN Security Council Resolution 2803 with 16-17 commissioners led by Ali Shaath, and the 15-point plan would make it custodian of decommissioned weapons. Report what it actually controls: its budget and who funds it, whether it pays Gaza's civil servants and teachers, what permits it issues, how its authority stops at the Yellow Line, and its legal relationship to the PA ministries in Ramallah. Attribute every mandate to the resolution text or a named official, and separate powers on paper from powers exercised.

topics.en: Gaza's chronic patients lose clinics to the restricted-access zone
topics.ar: مرضى غزة المزمنون يفقدون عياداتهم داخل منطقة الوصول المقيّد
topics.q: OCHA put Gaza's restricted-access zone at 64.9 per cent of the Strip by June 2026, up from about 53 per cent at the October ceasefire. Report the health consequence with a solutions lens: which dialysis units, cancer and diabetes clinics and pharmacies now sit east of the Yellow Line, how many patients that strands (attribute to the health ministry, WHO and MSF by statement and date), and what the workarounds are — mobile units, relocated dialysis chairs, medicine runs, telemedicine consults. Name what is delivered, funded, underway and still needed.

topics.en: Israeli commentators argue over annexation before the October vote
topics.ar: معلقون إسرائيليون يتجادلون حول الضم قبل انتخابات أكتوبر
topics.q: Read the Hebrew commentariat on annexation as an election issue: who in Ynet, Maariv, Israel Hayom and Haaretz argues for sovereignty over Area C, who warns of the cost, and which party platforms carry it. Attribute every argument to its named author and outlet, label think tanks (INSS, JISS, Misgav) with their lean, and keep house language — the occupied West Bank, never Judea and Samaria outside a quote. Frame the Palestinian stake: what each position would do to permits, land registration and movement.

topics.en: Israeli newsrooms audit their own anonymous security sourcing
topics.ar: غرف أخبار إسرائيلية تراجع اعتمادها على مصادر أمنية مجهولة
topics.q: Ynet's self-audit counted alarming stories sourced to anonymous security officials, most of which resurfaced in Netanyahu's speeches. Report the media-accountability file: which claims were published, which were later contradicted, what the Press Council and the army spokesman say about access and embargoes (the Qusra access complaint is the recent case), and what it means for Palestinian readers reading Israeli reporting about their own towns. Attribute each item to author, outlet and date.

topics.en: Congress writes Israel's aid lines into the next spending bill
topics.ar: الكونغرس يكتب بنود المساعدات لإسرائيل في موازنته المقبلة
topics.q: Track the appropriations and NDAA text as the American papers and think tanks report it: the military-aid lines, the UNRWA restrictions, any Gaza reconstruction money, and the Iran-war supplemental competing with all of it. Name each outlet and author inline, label think tanks with their lean (WINEP, FDD, Quincy, Arab Center DC), and convert every figure into what it funds or withholds on the ground. Attribute all numbers to the bill text or a named official.

topics.en: Washington's papers weigh what recognition of Palestine changed
topics.ar: صحف واشنطن تقيس ما غيّرته الاعترافات بدولة فلسطين
topics.q: A year after the wave of recognitions, read how the American press and Washington's think tanks assess them ahead of UNGA week: what changed in law, trade, embassies and aid, what the administration did in response, and which arguments each shop makes. One source piece per story, opinion attributed to its author, think tanks labelled. Pair with the paper's own recognition audit rather than repeating it.

topics.q: Practical bitchat reporting for a connectivity war: what the current release adds, how the mesh behaves in dense urban blocks and camps, battery cost, range in real tests worldwide, and documented disaster and blackout deployments. Every piece carries the official-download-only guidance (App Store 'bitchat mesh', id 6748219622, Permissionless Technology; the permissionlesstech GitHub APK for Android; Google Play hosts impostors). The ecash/Cashu side stays with the Financial Freedom desk.

topics.en: Palestinian families count what sending money home costs them
topics.ar: عائلات فلسطينية تحسب كلفة إرسال المال إلى الوطن
topics.q: Report the actual cost of moving money into the West Bank and Gaza: bank and exchange-house spreads, transfer fees, the shekel-dollar conversion, delays and refusals, and the compliance rules that produce them, attributed to the Palestine Monetary Authority, World Bank data and named operators with dates. Then the alternatives, described plainly and without advocacy — mobile wallets, stablecoins, ecash — with the legal and volatility risks stated in the same breath. No investment advice, ever.

topics.en: Palestine's week in numbers holds the record institutions publish
topics.ar: أسبوع فلسطين بالأرقام يجمع ما تنشره المؤسسات
topics.q: A weekly numbers piece built only from published institutional records: OCHA's displacement and settler-violence counts, the health ministry's casualty and hospital figures, the prisoners' institutions' tallies, PCBS economic releases and the Palestine Exchange close. Every figure carries the body that published it and the date, movements are compared with the previous week's release, and nothing is estimated. Say plainly which institution did not publish that week.

topics.en: Crossings and permits decide who moves in Palestine this week
topics.ar: المعابر والتصاريح تحدد من يتحرك في فلسطين هذا الأسبوع
topics.q: The movement file as a standing news service: which crossings opened and for whom (Rafah, Kerem Shalom, Allenby, the West Bank checkpoints), the weekly medical-exit and student-exit quotas, permit approvals and refusals, and the closures announced for holidays or operations. Attribute each figure to COGAT statements, WHO and OCHA updates, the crossings authority or named officials, with dates, and report the human consequence in wire-service register.

topics.en: Egypt and Jordan train the police force that will hold Gaza
topics.ar: مصر والأردن تدرّبان الشرطة التي ستضبط غزة
topics.q: The stabilization force's commander pairs 20,000 foreign soldiers with 12,000 Palestinian police trained in Egypt and Jordan. Report the police half as its own file: who recruits and vets them, who commands them on the ground, what law they enforce and under whose authority — the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, the Board of Peace, or the PA's interior ministry — how many have finished training, and where they deploy first. Attribute every number to the named official or institution with a date, including Egypt's foreign ministry on the 5,000-officer programme and the EU mission's role, and treat whether Palestinians command their own police as the reporting question rather than an assumption.

topics.en: Gaza's reconstruction ledger: what actually got rebuilt this month
topics.ar: دفتر إعمار غزة.. ما الذي أعيد بناؤه فعلاً هذا الشهر
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable monthly. The rebuild-by-the-numbers file: housing units repaired or rebuilt vs the assessed need (UN-Habitat/UNDP shelter cluster by report and date), rubble cleared vs the estimated tonnage, schools and clinics reopened, materials that entered via each crossing this month, and one named neighborhood's before/after carried as ground truth. Constructive framing per charter: credit delivered work precisely; distinguish promised, funded, underway, completed and still needed.

topics.en: Who becomes a guardian in Gaza, and who registers it
topics.ar: من يصير وصيّاً في غزة.. ومن يسجّل ذلك؟
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable; research fresh each run. The guardianship file behind the orphan counts: the Ministry of Social Development's registry and its latest figure with date, UNICEF's unaccompanied-and-separated caseload, the IRC's identification/tracing/registration gap, how kafala and kinship care are documented when the registries were destroyed, what allowance (if any) a host household receives, and whether adolescents are placed at all. Report the issue, never the individual; never name or identify a child. Every number attributed to its ministry, agency or report with a date.

topics.en: What holds a Palestinian refugee camp together when its services fail
topics.ar: ما الذي يمسك مخيماً فلسطينياً حين تتعطّل خدماته؟
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable across camps in the West Bank, Gaza, Lebanon, Syria and Jordan. The social institutions that carry a camp when UNRWA funding, municipal services or clinics fail: popular committees, mutual-aid funds, the women's centres, the schools' parent bodies, and the youth clubs. Verify UNRWA's current funding and service position at writing (by statement and date), name the camp and its committee, and credit delivered work precisely per the constructive-framing rule while stating plainly what has stopped.

topics.en: Marriage, birth and household formation under Gaza's ceasefire
topics.ar: الزواج والولادة وتكوين الأسرة في ظلّ وقف النار
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable. The demographic and social record the war rewrote: PCBS marriage, divorce and birth registrations before and after October 2023 (by release and date), what a wedding costs now, where couples live when the housing stock is rubble, maternal-care capacity for the births that follow, and the female-headed-household share. Numbers attributed to PCBS, the health ministry, UNFPA or UN Women with their dates; issue-not-individual discipline throughout.

topics.en: Palestinian writers argue the questions their institutions avoid
topics.ar: كتّاب فلسطينيون يجادلون في ما تتجنّبه مؤسساتهم
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable. A signed argument on a live Palestinian question, written for this paper and labelled as opinion: the argument is the writer's, made on the documented record, with the counter-case stated fairly and in its strongest form. Rotating subject territory — representation and the PLO's institutions, the shape of any post-war administration in Gaza, what recognition changed, the diaspora's political role. Never anonymous, never the paper's voice, never an attack on an individual; office-holders are argued with on their record.

topics.en: The Gaza roadmap's fine print deserves a Palestinian reading
topics.ar: البنود الصغيرة في خارطة غزة تستحق قراءة فلسطينية
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable as the roadmap moves. A signed analytical argument reading the current text of the Board of Peace roadmap, the stabilisation-force mandate and the reconstruction-fund rules from a Palestinian legal and political standpoint: what each clause obliges, who verifies it, what it omits, and which Palestinian body has standing anywhere in it. Quote the document, date the version being read, attribute every reading to its author, and carry the strongest counter-argument.

topics.en: Israel calls every strike pre-emption and the ceasefire keeps counting dead
topics.ar: تقصف باسم التهديد الوشيك.. من يحاكم غارات ما بعد وقف النار؟
topics.q: Report the doctrine that governs Israeli fire during the ceasefire. Kushner and Netanyahu agreed in Jerusalem on 17 August 2026 to a deconfliction mechanism assessing whether Israeli claims of emerging Hamas threats are genuine or resolvable without force, with Kushner saying Israel should not define 'imminent threats' too broadly (Channel 12 and Axios, citing a senior US official). Establish: how many of the 1,265-plus Palestinians killed since 10 October (Gaza health ministry) died in strikes Israel justified as pre-emption, and how those justifications were worded; what the October ceasefire text and Security Council resolution 2803 actually permit; who sits in the new mechanism and whether any Palestinian body can contest a finding; and what remedy exists for a family whose home was hit on a threat assessment later shown to be wrong. Every strike attributed to the army's own statement and date; every count to the institution that made it. Titles active voice, naming the actor.

topics.en: Central America's Palestinian communities carry the cause into national politics
topics.ar: جاليات فلسطين في أميركا الوسطى تحمل القضية إلى سياسة بلادها
topics.q: Report the Palestinian communities of Honduras, El Salvador and Guatemala — overwhelmingly descended from Christian families who left Bethlehem, Beit Jala and Beit Sahour under Ottoman and British rule — and what they are doing for Palestine now. Establish with sources: community size estimates and who produced them; the institutions (clubs, chambers of commerce, churches, cultural centres) and when each was founded; the documented political interventions since October 2023 — recognition votes, ICJ interventions, aid convoys, medical evacuations, scholarship funds — each attributed and dated. Celebratory register per the features order for the community's story and achievements; where a business or political figure of Palestinian descent is discussed, report the record precisely and never treat descent itself as an argument. Carry the honest line on distance: several of these communities are four and five generations from Palestine and many members have never been able to visit. Both editions; Arabic composed fresh.

topics.en: Diaspora families spend years on paperwork to bring relatives out of Gaza
topics.ar: عائلات المهجر تلاحق الأوراق سنوات لإخراج أقاربها من غزة
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable as the rules change. Report the administrative machine a diaspora Palestinian meets when trying to reunify with family in Gaza: which states run a Gaza family-reunification route and on what terms (Ireland, Canada, Germany, Egypt's coordination fees, the United States' humanitarian parole picture), what documents are demanded of an applicant whose civil registry office was destroyed, who controls exit through Rafah and Kerem Shalom at the time of writing, and what the recorded processing times and approval rates are. Every rule attributed to the ministry or agency that published it, with the date of the version described; costs stated in the currency charged. Report the issue, never the individual — a family's case runs only with consent and only in the detail it agrees to. Both editions; Arabic composed fresh.

topics.en: Recognition without a consulate is a sentence, not a policy
topics.ar: اعتراف بلا قنصلية: جملة سياسية لا سياسة
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable as recognitions accumulate. A signed argument, made on the documented record, about what the states that recognised Palestine have actually changed in law, trade, visas, diplomatic representation and arms licensing since recognising — and what recognition obliges next. Name each state and the instrument it did or did not amend, with dates; distinguish what is promised, funded, underway and delivered per the charter's constructive-framing rule. The counter-case — that recognition is a legal fact whose effects are necessarily slow, and that demanding immediate consequences devalues it — must be stated in its strongest form. Signed, never the paper's voice, never an attack on an individual.

topics.en: Palestinians should argue openly about the clearance revenue trap
topics.ar: آن للفلسطينيين أن يتجادلوا علناً في مصيدة المقاصة
topics.q: Evergreen keeper topic — recyclable as the fiscal crisis moves. A signed argument on the Paris Protocol arrangement that lets Israel collect two-thirds of Palestinian public revenue and withhold it at will: whether the Authority should keep operating inside it, what a refusal would cost in salaries and services, what alternatives have actually been proposed (a Palestinian customs authority, direct donor budget support, a shekel exit, correspondent banking outside Israeli banks) and who has costed them. Every figure attributed to the World Bank, IMF, Palestine Monetary Authority or the finance ministry with its date; market and fiscal levels are facts, never advice. Carry the strongest counter-argument — that 140,000 salaries make experimentation unaffordable — in full. Signed, never the paper's voice.

topics.en: What the E1 tender does to travel between Ramallah and Hebron
topics.ar: ماذا يفعل عطاء «إي 1» بالطريق بين رام الله والخليل؟
topics.q: The movement file behind the E1 settlement tender opened on 18 August 2026 for 1,234 housing units, bids closing 19 October: report it as a road map rather than a symbol. Which Palestinian routes between the northern and southern West Bank survive if E1 is built, how long each detour adds today (the Wadi al-Nar road, the container checkpoint, the Ma'ale Adumim ring), what the plan does to the Bedouin communities in the corridor including Khan al-Ahmar, and where the 3,401 planned units sit relative to Jerusalem's municipal boundary. Attribute every figure and map claim to Peace Now, Ir Amim, OCHA, B'Tselem or the Israel Land Authority tender with its date; carry the pending legal challenge and any Israeli state response. Track the American record too — the June 2026 letter from 85 members of Congress to Secretary Rubio and the administration's stated non-position — without turning the file into a Washington story.

topics.en: Gaza's music teachers rebuild lessons without buildings or instruments
topics.ar: معلّمو الموسيقى في غزة يعيدون الدروس بلا مبانٍ ولا آلات
topics.q: How music teaching in Gaza is being reassembled after the war: the Edward Said National Conservatory of Music's Gaza branch and what remains of it, teachers running lessons in tents, shelters and online, instruments donated and instruments lost, the oud and qanun workshops, and the children's choirs that reformed. Celebratory register per the features order — the teachers' work is the story, not an audit of an institution. Attribute every number (students enrolled, branches damaged, instruments replaced) to the conservatory, the culture ministry or the named NGO with its date, and carry what is funded, underway and still needed separately. Name the musicians who are teaching, with their consent, and let their words lead.

topics.en: Palestine builds a Paralympic squad from a generation of amputees
topics.ar: فلسطين تبني منتخباً بارالمبياً من جيل فقد أطرافه
topics.q: The Paralympic file ahead of Los Angeles 2028: the Palestinian Paralympic Committee's programmes, which sports have classified athletes (athletics, powerlifting, table tennis, sitting volleyball, wheelchair basketball), the training grounds that survive in Gaza and the West Bank, prosthetics and wheelchair supply as a sporting question, and the classification and travel obstacles that keep athletes from qualification events. Peg to the amputation estimates from WHO and the health ministry, attributed with dates, and to the PFA's facility and casualty counts. Celebratory register per the features order: the athletes' work is the story. Carry Olympic Solidarity and IPC support precisely — promised, funded, delivered — and be honest about what is not yet in place.

topics.en: The technicians who learned to build limbs while the war ran
topics.ar: فنيّون تعلّموا صناعة الأطراف بينما الحرب دائرة
topics.q: A Real Lives profile of the Palestinian prosthetics and orthotics technicians trained since 2023 — who they were before, where they trained (Gaza's own workshops, Jordan, Egypt, Türkiye, online mentoring from abroad), what a socket fitting costs in time and material now, and how they work through power cuts and closed supply lines. Named, consenting subjects; their words lead and our summary follows. Celebratory register per the features order: the achievement is the story. Attribute every count of amputations and fittings to WHO, the health ministry, MSF or the ICRC with its date, and distinguish devices delivered from devices pledged.

topics.en: Israel renews detention orders faster than courts review them
topics.ar: الاحتلال يجدّد أوامر الاعتقال الإداري أسرع من مراجعتها
topics.q: The renewal mechanism inside administrative detention, reported as machinery rather than as a total: how an order is issued and by whom, the confirmation hearing and what a detainee's lawyer may see of the secret file, how often orders are renewed and for how long, the practice of re-arrest after release, and the child and female detainee counts kept separately. Every figure attributed to the specific institution and date — نادي الأسير, هيئة شؤون الأسرى, HaMoked, B'Tselem, the Israel Prison Service's own published counts — and any Israeli official response carried. Report the issue, never the individual; a woman detainee's account keeps Her Story's consent-and-safety rules.

topics.en: Arab medical corridors moved patients out; the count says how many
topics.ar: الممرات الطبية العربية أخرجت مرضى.. والأرقام تقول كم
topics.q: An audit of the Arab medical corridors for Gaza patients: Egypt's Rafah and El-Arish route, Jordan's air bridge and field hospitals, the Emirati and Qatari evacuations, Saudi and Kuwaiti funded treatment, and the Yemeni and Algerian scholarship-linked medical places. For each: patients evacuated with dates, hospitals and beds actually operating, money pledged against money disbursed, and who verifies the count. Constructive framing per the charter — credit delivered work precisely, separate promised from funded from underway from completed, and name what is still needed as the next practical stage. Every figure attributed to the named ministry, WHO, or the hospital operator with its date.

topics.en: Gaza's hospitals wait while the money that moved trained police
topics.ar: مستشفيات غزة تنتظر.. والمال الذي تحرّك درّب الشرطة
topics.q: An audit of Gaza's health-sector reconstruction financing since the Board of Peace pledging meeting in Washington on 19 February 2026. Establish, with dates and named sources: the health share of the World Bank-UN-EU damage assessment published on 20 April 2026; which hospitals, clinics, dialysis and oncology units have actually been rebuilt, repaired or reopened, by whom and with whose money; and how much of the $17 billion pledged has been transferred, with the share of it that reached a health facility. Set that against the $100 million the United Arab Emirates transferred for police training and the $206 million the State Department notified to Congress on 30 July 2026 for the International Stabilization Force. Name the operators — WHO, the Gaza health ministry, MSF, the Jordanian and Emirati field hospitals, the Palestine Red Crescent Society — and attribute every figure to the institution and its date. Constructive framing per the charter: credit delivered work precisely, separate promised from funded from underway from completed, and present the gap as the next practical stage. Report the issue, never the individual patient.
